description: A festival jury coordinator must approve the final screening and deliberation protocol for a competition documentary, including playback format, accessibility presentation, projection settings, recording rules, and press access.

shared_context.S1: The competition documentary is scheduled for a private jury screening at the festival's 2:00 PM screening block on Saturday.
shared_context.S2: The jury will deliberate immediately after the screening in the same cinema.
shared_context.S3: Mara has final authority to approve the screening and deliberation protocol.
shared_context.S4: The festival's normal package-signoff routine is a round-robin check with distributor relations, accessibility, projection, and legal before Mara publishes the final protocol.

PF1.text: Jonas reviewed the countersigned distributor license this morning and confirmed that the film may be shown to the closed festival jury only from an encrypted DCP played offline; the license prohibits a cloud stream or an unencrypted screening file. He has not entered the restriction in the festival package because the signed license is still being indexed.

PF2.text: Leila's accessibility review with the film's caption vendor confirmed that this documentary must use English open captions burned into the picture, and the package must reserve four front-row seats for jury members who need caption visibility. She has not updated the standard accessibility template because the vendor returned the confirmation after the template was circulated.

PF3.text: Victor's projector test confirmed that this film's approved master must be played at exactly 25 fps with the cinema's 2K DCP ingest profile; the available 24 fps fallback produces audio drift by the final reel. He has not changed the auditorium preset because the screening is still listed under the festival's default profile.

PF4.text: Nadia's review of the jury confidentiality agreement confirmed that the deliberation may not be audio-recorded or video-recorded, and that accredited press may enter only after deliberation ends at 5:00 PM. She has not amended the event brief because the signed confidentiality pages arrived in legal's inbox after the brief was drafted.

acceptance_conditions: The film must be screened from an encrypted DCP played offline.
The screening must use English open captions burned into the picture.
Exactly four front-row seats must be reserved for caption visibility.
The film must be projected at exactly 25 fps using the 2K DCP ingest profile.
The jury deliberation must have no audio or video recording.
Press access must begin exactly at 5:00 PM after deliberation ends.
The final package must include commitments documenting the rights, accessibility, projection, and confidentiality requirements.

content_checks.C2: decisions['caption_mode'] == 'English open captions burned into picture'

decisive_facts.why: The countersigned license changes the playback choice from an ordinary festival file or stream to an encrypted DCP played offline and requires the rights-compliance commitment.

The vendor confirmation changes caption presentation to English open captions burned into the picture, fixes the reserved-seat count at exactly four, and requires the accessibility-reservation commitment.
The projector test changes the technical settings from the default 24 fps profile to exactly 25 fps with the 2K DCP ingest profile and requires the projection-configuration commitment.
The confidentiality agreement changes deliberation recording to none and moves press access to exactly 5:00 PM, requiring the confidentiality-control commitment.
